cool-white.purpose: Base surface, and the text color on inverted ink surfaces. Deliberately not pure white — green-tinted cold white so ink and cobalt read as printed rather than screen-lit.

cool-white-shade.purpose: Alternating surface, used only to separate adjacent project cards in the sticky stack.

cool-ink.purpose: Body text, full-strength hairlines, and the two inverted block surfaces (final project card, contact section).

ink-secondary.purpose: Secondary and descriptive copy — ledes, list descriptions, timeline detail.

ink-muted.purpose: Metadata that should recede — row numbers, section glosses, period labels, the inactive language chip, registration crosses. Measures 4.62:1 on cool white, clearing AA at the 11–12px sizes it is used at. Was #7f8985 (3.35:1) until the July 2026 pass, where it failed the project's own standard while carrying work-history dates and certification years. Recession is the lightest legible step, not an illegible one.

hairline.purpose: The 64px drafting grid and dividers internal to a section. An alpha token over the base surface — no tonal ramp applies.
hairline.note: Alpha-over-surface token; use cool-ink's ramp for solid equivalents.

hairline-strong.purpose: Structural rules — between sections, under section heads, between the two sector columns.
hairline-strong.note: Alpha-over-surface token; use cool-ink's ramp for solid equivalents.

electric-cobalt.purpose: The line weight of a technical drawing. Structure: section indices, the asterisk mark, schematic edges and pulses, the availability stamp, the timeline rail, growing nav underlines, the photo's offset overprint, focus rings on light grounds.

cobalt-deep.purpose: Hover state for cobalt objects only. No independent role.

acid-green.purpose: The highlighter. Pulse: sector tags, LIVE status, hero role words, photo caption, active language chip, the second marquee band, ::selection, contact underline, current timeline markers, the LLM node. Used as a ground beneath ink text, not as text.

display.purpose: The hero name, two lines in a single left-aligned block, uppercase. Its close relative at 680 weight / wdth 112% and clamp(44px, 8vw, 112px) is the contact heading.

display-contact.purpose: The contact heading ("OZVĚTE SE."), uppercase. The largest type on the page and the page's end frame — heavier and wider than the hero name at wdth 112%.

headline.purpose: Project names on the deck cards. Mixed case, not uppercase — these are proper nouns and read as marks.

address.purpose: The contact e-mail. Archivo at 500 weight and wdth 100% — lighter and narrower than any other display use, because it is an address rather than a headline.

title.purpose: Section headings. Always paired with a cobalt mono index to the left and a hairline beneath.

subtitle.purpose: Competency row titles, sector column headings, timeline roles (fixed 19px at line-height 1.3).

body.purpose: Running copy at 17px/1.65. Measure capped per block: 52–58ch descriptions, ~56ch ledes, ~22ch display-set headings.

body-lede.purpose: The hero summary paragraph and other opening copy, one step up from body.

body-small.purpose: Descriptive copy inside dense structures — register descriptions, timeline detail, definition lists.

role.purpose: Timeline job titles at a fixed 19px — Archivo at wdth 105%, the smallest display use on the page.

body-meta.purpose: Definition-list values in the About sidebar at 15px: education, certification, languages.

glyph.purpose: The scroll-progress asterisk at 24px. A glyph size, not a text step.

glyph-lg.purpose: The stamp's centre asterisk at 44px inside the SVG. A glyph size, not a text step.

label.purpose: The .mono utility. Every index, tag, URL, status, period and nav item. Variants: wordmark 13px/600 at 0.1em; nav 11.5px/500 at 0.09em; marquee 13px/500 at 0.12em; stamp text 13.5px/600 at 0.2em; footer 11px at 0.05em in sentence case — the one place mono is not uppercased.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The system's only easing token (--ease-out). Fast out, long settle. Used for every transform and background-size transition.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: Opacity + 18px translateY on [data-reveal] elements, triggered by IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.15 with rootMargin 0px 0px -8% 0px. Gated behind the .js class so content is visible without JS.

motion.name: reveal-stagger
motion.purpose: transition-delay multiplied by the element's --i index. The floor obligation for any new section. At --i:4 the last row reaches full opacity in ~980ms.

motion.name: hero-rise
motion.purpose: One-shot 0.3em rise + fade on the hero name at load.

motion.name: underline-grow
motion.purpose: background-size from 0% to 100% on a 1px currentColor gradient — the standard text-link affordance. Nav variant is 240ms on a 2px cobalt gradient.

motion.name: micro-shift
motion.purpose: translate(3px, -3px) on the ↗ glyph of external links; translateX(14px) at 320ms on register row titles.

motion.name: state-color
motion.purpose: Plain color and border-color transitions on hover. Linear ease, no custom curve.

motion.name: stamp-spin
motion.purpose: Base rotation of the availability stamp, plus a scroll-velocity increment accumulated into the --boost custom property.

motion.name: scroll-lerp
motion.purpose: Smoothing factor applied to scroll velocity in the single rAF loop (smoothV += (v - smoothV) * 0.12). Drives band acceleration, stamp boost, and schematic pulse rate.

motion.name: band-drift
motion.purpose: Base marquee speed before scroll acceleration; direction from the data-band attribute (-1 left, 1 right). Normalized to 60fps via a dt factor capped at 3.

motion.name: schematic-draw
motion.purpose: Canvas schematic build-in: edges draw from the hub via lineDashOffset, nodes fade in 120ms apart over 300ms. Complete inside 2s. DPR capped at 2.

breakpoints.name: hero
breakpoints.purpose: Hero grid collapses to one column; stamp repositions to 104px at the corner.

breakpoints.name: about
breakpoints.purpose: About grid collapses to one column.

breakpoints.name: register
breakpoints.purpose: Competency rows drop to 48px 1fr; description reflows under the title.

breakpoints.name: nav
breakpoints.purpose: Nav reduces to Projects + Contact; sectors stack and swap their dividing hairline from left border to top border.

breakpoints.name: head
breakpoints.purpose: Section-head gloss hides and the head wraps; deck cards grow to 70vh.

accessibility.focus: 2px solid cobalt at 3px offset on light grounds; acid inside ink sections. Deck cards use a 2px inset cobalt outline via :focus-within because the click target is a full-bleed overlay.
accessibility.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all durations to 0.01ms, stops the stamp, sets the timeline line to scaleY(1), clears band and glyph transforms, and renders the schematic complete and pulse-free. The result is a full static drawing, not a degraded page.
accessibility.noJs: html:not(.js) renders the timeline line complete; reveal and hero-rise animations are gated behind the .js class so all content is visible without JS.
accessibility.decorative: Canvas schematic, marquee bands and stamp glyphs are aria-hidden; the bands carry an sr-only paragraph with the same content in reading order.
accessibility.statusRedundancy: Status is encoded three ways at once — glyph (● ◐ ○), border treatment (filled / solid / dashed) and color — so it survives without color perception.

narrative.overview:
Modrotisk is the Czech word for indigo-resist block printing — a folk textile craft where a resist paste is stamped onto cloth, the cloth is dipped in indigo, and the pattern emerges as bright figures on a deep blue ground. Read literally, the same word decomposes into modrý + tisk: blue print. Both readings are load-bearing here. From the craft comes the discipline of a stamped mark, a registration that either aligns or visibly does not, and ink that sits in the surface rather than floating above it. From the literal reading comes the drafting table: a 64px grid, orthogonal elbow joins as in an ArchiMate diagram, registration crosses at the corners of every node, cobalt as the line weight of a technical drawing.

The system is bright, cool and orthogonal. Cool white ground, cool-black ink, one structural blue and one highlighter green. Depth is achieved by offset and hairline rather than by blur: the About photograph carries a cobalt frame displaced 12px down and right, exactly as a misregistered second pass would print. There are no shadows anywhere in the stylesheet, no gradients other than the grid's own fade-out mask, no grain, no glass. Nothing is rounded except two things that are literally circles — the availability stamp and the scroll-progress button.

The counter-position is explicit and was the reason for the redesign. This replaced a dark, Raycast-inspired v4 whose genre — dark ground, glow blobs, a grid of hairline-bordered cards, five rainbow accents, mono eyebrow labels — is now the default output of any code-generating model. It also replaced an intermediate v5 ("Papír a stroj": warm paper, Fraunces, vermilion) rejected for sepia tones and typographic overacting. Brightness is the first differentiator; the second is that the graphics carry meaning. The hero's animated canvas schematic says solution architect without a word of copy, and it earns the space a decorative illustration would have wasted.

On the status of what follows: every rule in this system describes the shipped v5.1 implementation and holds until a deliberate decision replaces it. None of them is sacred. They are named and stated forcefully because a design system that hedges gets ignored, not because they are beyond revision — a future direction is free to overturn any of them, as long as it does so on purpose and system-wide rather than by drift on one section.
keyCharacteristics: Bright cool-white ground; dark surfaces are the rare exception, not the mode
Exactly two accents, each with one job: cobalt structures, acid pulses
Zero radius everywhere except literal circles; zero shadows anywhere
Depth by offset overprint and hairline, never by blur
Full-bleed hairlines set the vertical rhythm; sections are separated by rules, not cards
Three type roles on three faces: Archivo display, Instrument Sans text, Spline Sans Mono meta
Graphics are technical artifacts (grid, registration crosses, stamp, schematic), not ornament
Scroll produces motion in several directions and speeds at once; prefers-reduced-motion yields a complete static drawing

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: Cobalt structures, acid pulses. A third accent hue would require deciding what job it does, and there is no third job. When a new element needs color, it is asking to be either structure or pulse; decide which, then use that accent.

rules.name: The Acid Never Speaks Rule
rules.body: Acid is a ground or an underline, never a text color. As text on cool white it measures 1.11:1 — invisible. As a ground under cool ink it measures 15.5:1. The rule is a legibility fact wearing a doctrine's clothes.

rules.name: The Two Ink Blocks Rule
rules.body: The inverted ink surface appears twice on the page — the final project card and the contact section — and it lands because it is rare. A third would make the page look like it has a dark theme it does not have.

rules.name: The Inverse Opacity Ladder
rules.body: On ink surfaces, secondary text is cool white at 0.75, metadata at 0.6, muted at 0.5, and borders at 0.25. These are written as literal rgba(245, 247, 246, …) in the stylesheet rather than as tokens; treat the ladder as the token until it is promoted into one.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: Display type is set on Archivo's wdth axis between 105% and 115%, wider as it gets larger. Reaching for more presence means going wider and heavier, not just bigger — the axis is what distinguishes this setting from any default sans at a big size.

rules.name: The Third Voice Rule
rules.body: Every piece of metadata is mono, uppercase, and tracked open. Anything that is a label, an index, a URL, a status, or a date belongs to Spline Sans Mono; anything a person reads as a sentence belongs to Instrument Sans. There is no overlap, which is what keeps the two from competing. The footer is the one place mono is not uppercased.

rules.name: The Czech Typography Rule
rules.body: Correct Czech typesetting is a requirement, not a finish: „low-high quotes", em dashes, non-breaking spaces after single-letter prepositions and inside broken numerals and coordinates, and no orphans in headings. The English mutation follows English conventions with the same rigor. Both files carry these as literal entities in the markup.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Card Rule
rules.body: Structure is expressed with lines across the page. When a new block needs separating, give it a hairline and vertical space; do not give it a border box, a background panel, or a radius.

rules.name: The Own-Proportion Rule
rules.body: Each section declares the grid its content wants. Consistency lives in the gutter, the container, the rules, and the type — not in a shared column count.

rules.name: The Offset-Not-Blur Rule
rules.body: Depth is produced by displacing a line, changing a tone, or stacking a real surface. A shadow would introduce a light source the page has otherwise decided not to have.

rules.name: The Two-Radii Rule
rules.body: 0 for anything rectangular, 50% for anything that is a physical round object. No 4px, no 8px, no pills.

rules.name: The Orthogonal Rule
rules.body: Connections turn at right angles. No diagonals, no bezier curves, no organic paths.

dos: Do give each accent its one job: cobalt for structure (links, indices, rails, connections, focus), acid for pulse (chips, live status, underlines, selection).

Do put acid behind ink text rather than in it — as a ground or an underline. The one exception in the system, acid text on an ink ground in the active language chip, works because the contrast is 15.5:1.
Do separate blocks with a full-bleed hairline and vertical space. --line-strong for structure, --line for internal dividers.
Do set display type on Archivo's width axis (105–115%) as well as its weight when it needs more presence.
Do keep every label, index, URL, status and date in Spline Sans Mono, uppercase, tracked at 0.08em or wider.
Do cap measure per block — 52–58ch for descriptions, ~56ch for ledes, ~22ch for display-set headings.
Do create depth by offsetting a line, changing a tone, or stacking a real surface.

Do give every new section the staggered reveal (data-reveal plus a --i index, 70ms apart over 700ms). A dedicated scroll behavior — a sticky stack, a self-drawing line — is earned by content that genuinely justifies one, not granted by default.
Do hide decorative motion from assistive technology (aria-hidden) and provide an sr-only equivalent whenever it carries real content.
Do encode status redundantly — glyph and border treatment and color, as in ● LIVE / ◐ BETA / ○ WIP.

Do run new motion through the single requestAnimationFrame loop in main.js, animate only transform and opacity, cache measurements outside the loop, and keep the try/catch so one bad frame cannot kill the sequence.
Do verify that prefers-reduced-motion leaves a complete, usable static page — the schematic fully drawn, the timeline line at full height, bands and glyphs untransformed.
Do keep the non-JS path intact: .js gates the reveal and rise animations, so content is visible when the class never lands.
donts: Don't add a third accent hue. If a new element needs color, decide whether it is structure or pulse and use that accent.
Don't introduce box-shadow, blur, backdrop filters, or grain. The page has decided not to have a light source.
Don't use a radius between 0 and 50%. No 4px, no 8px, no pills.
Don't enclose content in bordered boxes or background panels to group it — that was the v4 card-grid pattern this design replaced.
Don't add a third inverted ink surface. Two is what keeps them rare enough to register.
Don't tile the 64px drafting grid beyond the hero, where it fades out by design.
Don't draw a diagonal or curved connection. Elbows turn at right angles.
Don't put the photograph in the hero or crop it to a circle — it belongs in About, rectangular, grayscale, in its offset frame.

Don't let a decorative element overlap a meaning-carrying one. The stamp and the schematic are both cobalt; where they overlapped, a visitor read it as a rendering bug, not as intentional misregistration.
Don't place load-bearing text in --ink-3 at display sizes below 11px, and don't reintroduce a muted token that fails 4.5:1. Recession is the lightest legible step, not an illegible one.
